reviews.title: Slight of hand
reviews.text: Be warned.  If you sign up for this program, believing it is the chair exercise they advertised it would be, then discover that they pulled the wool over your eyes & it is not, it evidently cannot be canceled & your stuck paying for a product you cannot use.  There is ample warning for how much & what they will track, but clearly they don’t pay any attention to what or how often you use their product.  I am not able to get to the floor & back up, let alone get down to EXERCISE on the floor & back up!  But, by gum, Fit Me doesn’t care & keeps charging my account for that annual fee!  What are they tracking?  Certainly not me.  Maybe my internet footprint, but not my activity in Fit Me!  I thought I had gotten this canceled 11 months ago, but the charge came through again.  Not usually unreasonable, but when lied to, then have no way to contact anyone to discuss, I come apart.  Just be warned, y’all.

reviews.title: It does work and it does cost $$
reviews.text:
Yes, I think it does work. I wouldn’t say you’ll get a six-pack but you will get toned and I have had people notice a difference after about 4-6 weeks.

And it costs $$. I spent $20 for 30 days and then it auto-renewed at $50 for a 30 days before I cancelled. I got 57 days worth before it stopped and wanted me to ante up more, which I declined. If I had been offered $10/mo to continue after the first month I’d have probably sprung.

Don’t be so greedy, FitMe. And please take the word “lazy” out. I exercise five days/wk besides this but I saw the value in adding this. But my other exercises (e.g., road biking) are not indicative of laziness. And now I am doing other tai chi chair on YouTube that is free and so far, so good.
